Called around 22:00 for a dyspneic patient with worsening gas exchange P/F 149.

Reports burning chest pain already present for days. Effective productive cough with hemoptysis. Reports not taking medications and not suffering from any disease. Denies allergies. On the previous day ED visit for syncope following ingestion of a hot beverage.

Transferred for chest CT: In the CT angiography study, no signs of thromboembolic disease are evident. The aorta is of regular caliber. The right lung parenchyma shows multiple parenchymal consolidations, ubiquitously distributed but with predominant involvement of the basal pyramid, inflammatory in appearance, associated with a layer of pneumothorax, of irregular thickness with greater basal extension and with involvement of the interlobar fissure. The parenchyma, particularly the middle lobe, also shows numerous air-containing streaks, some of which extend to the interface with the pleural layers, from likely bronchial injury. On the left a few small consolidations are observed, more numerous at the level of the lower lobe, especially in the apical segment.

First discussion with the PARENTE, who are informed of the severity of the clinical situation.

Retransferred to the red code room; in agreement with attending Dr. NOME_PERSONA, the on-call thoracic surgeon (Dr. NOME_PERSONA) is contacted.

After collegial evaluation, blood cultures, urinary antigens, and initiation of antibiotic therapy are chosen (as reported in the ED note). Given the worsening respiratory function with tachypnea (>40 breaths/min) and need to increase O2 support (mask with reservoir FiO2 90%) and relative decline of saturation SpO2 87–88%, it is therefore decided collegially to proceed with ETI and subsequent placement of a chest drain.

New discussion with the PARENTE summarizing the therapeutic strategy.

After administration of Midazolam 2 mg, Fentanest 150 mcg, Etomidate 20 mg, and Rocuronium 100 mg with RSI technique, effective ETI on the second attempt with videolaryngoscope assistance, patient ventilated by mask. Dr. NOME_PERSONA called for help in clinical management. Upon placement of the ETT 8.0, EtCO2 present with bilateral breath sounds. Extreme difficulty with ventilation with va-e-vieni and desaturation (max SpO2 reached 82%). Impossibility for P picco of ventilation in VCV or protective PCV.

Sedation optimized with Propofol continuous infusion at 200 mg/h + Fentanest in repeated boluses (total 400 mcg), repeated curarization with Rocuronium 50 mg + Cisatracurium 10 mg. Also administered Hydrocortisone 100 mg, MgSO4 2 g, Ketamine 80 mg, Tranex 1 g, and 8 puffs of Ventolin. Hydrated with normal saline 1000 mL and subsequently electrolyte solution 500 mL. NOTE WRITTEN RETROSPECTIVELY FOR PATIENT ASSISTANCE.
Called for a 74-year-old patient, arrived in the ED accompanied by EMS for dyspnea and respiratory distress. On my arrival, patient very agitated, alert and conscious, but poorly cooperative.
Ventilated on NIV with PEEP 8, PS 7, FiO2 40%. SpO2 97%.
Solu-Medrol 125 mg already administered.
Patient tachypneic, with RR about 40 breaths/min. Respiratory mechanics with use of accessory abdominal muscles.
On venous blood gas, severe mixed acidosis with pH 6.96, pCO2 97.7, HCO3- 21.9, Lac 5.
Mottled skin, capillary refill about 4 seconds.
Hemodynamics with hypotensive BP 85/50 mmHg. An arterial line placed in the right radial artery.
Proceed to orotracheal intubation with RSI after sedation with Ketamine 100 mg, Fentanyl 100 mcg, and paralysis with Rocuronium 100 mg.
Using a video laryngoscope, a cuffed ETT size 8.0 was placed.
Subsequently Midazolam 5 mg administered and continuous infusion started at 5 mg/kg/h.
Patient connected to the ventilator and set to IPPV 540 mL x 22 with PEEP 8 cmH2O; FiO2 progressively reduced from 100% to 70%.
On auscultation inspiratory and expiratory wheezes, therefore MgSO4 2 g in 100 mL normal saline and Ventolin 4 puffs were administered.
Thamesol 1 vial also administered.
After induction worsening of hemodynamic instability and initiation of significant vasopressor support with norepinephrine with dose progressively increased up to 0.6 mcg/kg/min to obtain a MAP 60–65 mmHg.
On thoracic eFAST, B-lines throughout; on the left, a small pleural effusion and surrounding parenchymal consolidation with dynamic air bronchogram.
On cardiac eFAST, pericardial effusion of about 1.5 cm with compression of the right ventricle. Left heart hyperkinetic.
On ECG, likely injury pattern in inferior leads.
In light of the severe hemodynamic instability, together with the cardiology colleague it was decided to perform echo-guided pericardiocentesis.
Under sterile field, puncture via subxiphoid access. A total of about 20 mL of blood drained with slight improvement in BP values.
On ultrasound, marked reduction of the effusion.
Subsequently, under sterile field, a triple-lumen CVC was placed under ultrasound guidance in the right internal jugular vein.
The patient was then taken to CT to perform CT angiography of the chest and abdomen and cardiac CT: aortic dissection and cardiac rupture excluded on CT. Presence of a pericardial effusion of about 15 mm and left pleural effusion with a pulmonary picture of interstitial disease in paraseptal emphysema.
Also presence of a perisplenic fluid layer.
ETT slightly endobronchial to the right, therefore withdrawn by 1.5 cm.
On labs WBC 28,000, Hb 15.3, PLTs 281,000, INR 1.23, aPTT 31.8 s, Creatinine 1.4, AST 41, ALT 38, LDH 426, Na 143, K 4.2, CRP 11.9, Troponin T 1.6, CK 241.
Blood cultures drawn and empirical antibiotic therapy with levofloxacin started.
Approximately 2000 mL of crystalloids administered in total.
On return to the ED shock room, worsening of bronchospasm and hemodynamic instability.
On auscultation wheezes and grunting greater on the left and predominantly expiratory.
Ventolin 4 puffs and Ketamine 50 mg administered.
On blood gas, after partial compensation of respiratory acidosis up to pH 7.24, new worsening with pH 7.13, pCO2 63.6, pO2 59.3, HCO3- 21, Lac 1.81.
FiO2 returned to 100%.
Respiratory mechanics measured: Ppeak 41, Pplat 25, PEEP 8, total PEEP 14.
Ventilation modified setting the patient to IPPV 600 mL x 20 with PEEP 6 cmH2O. I:E ratio 1:3.
Total PEEP 9, Pplat 24.
Patient oliguric: diuresis 200 mL with concentrated urine.
On the last control blood gas pH 7.18, pCO2 57.9, pO2 63.6, HCO3- 21.1, Lac 1.71.
The patient was taken to the ICU to continue care.
diagnosis_phrase: aortic dissection and cardiac rupture excluded on CT. Presence of a pericardial effusion of about 15 mm and left pleural effusion with a pulmonary picture of interstitial disease in paraseptal emphysema. Also presence of a perisplenic fluid layer.

Given: Fentanyl 20 mcg

Status post radical cystectomy + creation of ileal conduit per Bricker.

ED presentation for lumbar pain onset several days ago.

No pleuropulmonary lesions with evolving appearance are documented. No hilar-mediastinal or axillary lymph nodes with short axis greater than 1 cm are observed, nor pleural or pericardial effusions. No current urgent urological indications.

clinical_note:
Written retrospectively to provide care to the patient.
72-year-old patient brought to the ED for acute onset of weakness of the left limbs.
PMH: No known allergies. COVID-19 vaccination series completed.

Reported past surgeries: bilateral carpal tunnel, meniscectomy.
Hypertension on therapy.
Dyslipidemia on therapy.
Type 2 DM on oral hypoglycemics.
Peripheral arterial disease of the lower limbs.
In 1990 duodenal ulcer reported, GERD.
COPD.
Ischemic heart disease treated in 1995 with double aortocoronary bypass and subsequently with angioplasty and stenting
Left breast neoplasm subjected to left quadrantectomy, underwent RT and hormone therapy.

HPI: on 8/10/21 ED visit at OMV for dyspnea where she was hospitalized two days for heart failure in CAD; discharged with indication for therapy with diuretics (furosemide and Luvion).
Home meds: Plavix 1 tab, simvastatin 40 mg 1 tab, metformin 1000 mg 1 tab x 3/day, ramipril 2.5 mg, metoprolol 100 mg 1/2 tab x 2/day, pantoprazole, Aliflus, Lasix 25 mg 1 tab x 2/day, Luvion 100 mg 1 tab at 16:00.

According to the PARENTE, already during the brief hospitalization for heart failure the PARENTE had dysarthric-type speech blocks ("mangled" some words). The disturbance lasted until 18/10 and in recent days left hemifacial paresthesias appeared, for which, on the treating physician's indication, she should have undergone an urgent neurology visit on 20/10.
She woke up on the morning of 19/10 in fair well-being around 08:00. At 08:30 while in the kitchen she suddenly called the PARENTE who was in the bathroom and then fell to the ground. The PARENTE heard the call and the thud but did not witness the fall. Found her on the ground with eyes closed and then with motor impairment of the left limbs. EMS called and brought to the ED. In the ED patient alert with head and eyes deviated to the right, mute and with weakness of the left limbs. BP = 230/120 mmHg.
Head CT with CT perfusion and CT angiography performed: on the right, faint right frontal hypodensities consistent with subacute ischemia, loss of gray-white matter differentiation in the right frontoparietal region + right MCA hyperdensity; large ischemic core in the right MCA territory and poor penumbra; on the left an atherosclerotic plaque at the bifurcation extending to involve the proximal segment of the internal carotid artery without significant stenosis, on the right an extensive atherosclerotic plaque involving the origin of the ICA causing tight stenosis, also detectable floating thrombus in the proximal segment of the right ICA + right MCA M1 occlusion with poor collateral circulation on delayed scans.
Neurological exam in CT: lies with eyes closed, but when called answers simple questions with single words, head and eyes deviated to the right. Left lower CN VII deficit. Left homonymous hemianopia. Mild dysarthria. Severe paresis of the left limbs (slight movements against gravity). Sensory deficits not clear. Left neglect.

Case discussed with the interventional radiology colleague with whom the neuroimages were reviewed; given the already ischemic findings on CT, no indications for acute treatments.

Upon return to the ED a bolus of labetalol was administered for BP persistently > 200/100 mmHg with good response 160/80 mmHg. Episodes of emesis reported by the patient.
The PARENTE was informed of the clinical picture.

Currently 11:00: patient still with eyes closed but turns the head toward the midline and to the left when called, but eyes deviated to the right. Does not produce sounds but follows some simple commands and answers with head nods. Plegia of the left limbs.

Impression: ischemia of the right MCA territory due to right MCA M1 thrombosis on an atherothrombotic basis (stenosing plaque + floating thrombus at the right ICA) in a patient with multiple vascular risk factors

Recommendations:
- Flectadol 1000 mg 1/4 fl in NS 100 cc + PPI
- BP control with cut-off 200/100 mmHg
- if possible perform chest X-ray
- admission to stroke unit as soon as a bed is available
diagnosis_phrase: ischemia of the right MCA territory due to right MCA M1 thrombosis on an atherothrombotic basis (stenosing plaque + floating thrombus at the right ICA) in a patient with multiple vascular risk factors

clinical_note:

On arrival patient on immobilization devices (cervical collar and spine board), alert, not fully cooperative, agitated; prehospital personnel reported a language barrier (speaks Portuguese). On palpation of the spine no palpable deformities, trachea midline, cervical collar correctly positioned.
Spontaneous ventilation without O2 support, SpO2 94-95% on RA, no visible deformities, no lacerations or penetrating wounds, no subcutaneous emphysema. Significant tenderness in the mid-chest and right chest (reported by EMS as present from the outset).
Effective autonomous circulation, BP 135/90 HR 105 bpm in sinus rhythm on monitor and ECG, no mottling, no bleeding sources, CRT<2’’. ABG (on room air): pH 7,4 pCO2 31,5 pO2 63 HCO3 19 Lac 2,25 Hb 15,6 Na 140 K+3,9. Extended-FAST: negative. Incidental finding of stomach filled with liquid material. 16 G PIV already in place in left forearm. A second access is placed in the right forearm.
GCS 12 (E3V3M6), anisocoria L>R present, motor function preserved in all four limbs as well as sensation.
No penetrating lacerations of the limbs, no color or temperature alterations.
Blood tests ordered, apertura TS, and whole-body CT with angio.
Administered fentanyl 100 mcg in repeated boluses for significant pain of difficult quantification, Ringer’s acetate 500 ml, Plasil 1 vial.

On CT: evidence of sternal fracture in multiple fragments and rib fractures without complications.

On head-to-toe reassessment
- neurocranium: Improvement of the neurological status GCS 13 (E4M6V3), reduction of anisocoria (but still present), no lacerations, no appreciable external bleeding sources, right frontal abrasion, no palpable lacerations of the scalp or face. No otorrhea. Reports improvement of pain after therapy (currently NRS 3). Right eyelid swelling.
- maxilla: No pain or deformity of bony profiles, no blood in the oral cavity, nor appreciable dental fragments
- mandible: normal mobility, no deformity
- neck: spine aligned, no profile deformities nor frank pain on palpation of the spinous processes, jugular veins not distended, trachea midline. Cervical collar removed after radiology report; cautious mobilization permitted without tenderness.
- chest: persistent central chest tenderness without deformities or hematomas, spontaneous ventilation without need for supplemental O2, SpO2 97% on RA, mild tachypnea (approx. RR 24/min), no subcutaneous emphysema.
- cardiovascular: effective and autonomous with unchanged parameters.
- abdomen: rounded, not tense, minimally tender, no evidence of hematomas in the hypochondrial regions, CT evidence of gastric dilatation. No nausea nor current vomiting.
- limbs: no appreciable bony deformities, normal color and temperature, good mobility.
- back: on log-roll no deformities of the spinous processes, wounds, or hematomas. Spine board removed and positioned at 30°.
Rapid SARS-CoV-2 antigen swab result: negative

Labs without significant abnormalities.

At the end of the joint management, the patient is entrusted to ED Medicine management in the absence of current resuscitation needs. We remain available.
diagnosis_phrase: sternal fracture in multiple fragments and rib fractures without complications

clinical_note:
CARDIOLOGY CONSULTATION
66-year-old patient, smoker 5 cigarettes/day, hypertensive, dyslipidemic

Ecofast EF normal 65% without segmental wall motion abnormalities, aortic root 27 mm, aortic arch 23 mm - ascending aorta not visualized due to thoracic conformation, mild MR; RV normal in size and motion. No pericardial effusion

In conclusion
Atypical chest pain during hypertensive crisis in a 66-year-old patient with hypertension, dyslipidemia
TnT negative at the first measurement. ECG diffuse abnormalities - SR - during hypertensive crisis
TTE normal EF, no wall motion abnormalities, aorta normal in the segments explored, RV normal, mild MR
Recommendations:

In the meantime optimize home therapy (currently bivis 20/5, omegastatin, atenolol 100 mg): increase BIVIS to 40/10 mg 1 tablet daily in the morning; atenolol in the evening; continue statin
Home BP monitoring is necessary
diagnosis_phrase: Atypical chest pain during hypertensive crisis in a 66-year-old patient with hypertension, dyslipidemia

clinical_note:

clinical_note:

I would recommend acetylsalicylic acid 300 mg now and subsequently 100 mg at lunch, ticagrelor 180 mg now and subsequently 90 mg at breakfast and dinner, pantoprazole 20 mg 1 tablet at breakfast, enoxaparin 100 U/kg at breakfast and dinner, bisoprolol 1.25 1 tablet now and subsequently 1 tablet at breakfast, furosemide 2 vials IV now and subsequently 1 vial at 08:00 and 20:00, Luvion 1 vial now and subsequently 1 vial at 16:00, nitroglycerin 2 vials in 250 cc at 5 mL/hour.
If stable, admission to the cardiology ward as soon as a bed is available.

Recommendations:
- now administer Decadron 8 mg IV + gastric protection; if necessary, add IV analgesic;
- at home: take deltacotene 50 mg 1 tab at 08:00 for 5 days, then taper to 25 mg 1 tab at 08:00 for another 4 days, then to 12.5 mg for another 4 days, and then resume the previous usual dose for the connective tissue disease;

clinical_note:

For about one week she has had subcontinuous headache, mostly pulsatile, starting from the cranial base and involving the whole head, bilateral, generally responsive to common NSAIDs.
She reports not usually suffering from headache; in the past she has had episodes of headache triggered by sexual intercourse.
For about one week conjunctivitis with yellowish palpebral secretions and foreign-body ocular sensation; 6 days ago she had a sensation of transient visual blurring in OU lasting 5 minutes.
For this reason she had an evaluation yesterday at the Ophthalmic Hospital where no particular problems were found.

This morning in the ED she underwent head CT + CTA of neck and intracranial vessels + intracranial CTV: negative.

Current neurological exam entirely within normal limits, no paresthesias, no hypoesthesia, no motor deficit in the 4 limbs, not even on segmental testing, no gait or balance deficits, no cerebellar deficits; DTRs brisk in the 4 limbs, symmetric; plantar reflex in flexion bilaterally; note Hoffmann positive on the left. Romberg negative.

Conclusions: headache; migrating paresthesias in the 4 limbs, positional.
Recommendation: Laroxyl 4 drops in the evening in abundant water for 4 days, then increase to 8 drops in the evening for another 4 days, then to 10 drops and continue like this for a few months.
If the paresthesias in the 4 limbs persist, recommend brain and cervico-dorsal MRI with and without contrast.

CT chest–abdomen: "There is exceedingly abundant ascites. The esophagus is hypotonic, with abundant liquid content. There is overdistension with predominantly liquid content of the gastric cavity and of the entire jejuno-ileal loops up to the level of involvement in the umbilical hernia (hernia orifice of about two centimeters). The loops distal to the umbilical hernia are without content, as is the colon. The finding is compatible with a torsion of a loop within the hernia. On EMS arrival the pt was alert but very agitated; administered midazolam 10 mg, then underwent orotracheal intubation (boluses of propofol and rocuronium). On arrival, head CT with CT angiography and perfusion was performed: no brain lesions, no occlusion/dissection/thrombosis of intracranial vessels, no perfusion abnormalities nor contrast enhancement.
Blood tests within normal limits, ethanol absent. Afebrile.
The pt was then extubated with progressive recovery of consciousness.
No chest pain nor dyspnea reported. ECG within normal limits.

Current neurologic exam: alert, oriented, cooperative. NNCC within normal limits. Ming I and II normal bilaterally. No language or sensory deficits. Finger-to-nose test normal bilaterally. No morsus.

Conclusion: probable first seizure with possible focal onset and secondary generalization.

At this time, no antiepileptic therapy is initiated.
Indicated:
- EEG (the pt will be called to perform it next week; present with referral)
- complete blood tests (CBC, hepatic and renal function, TSH R, QPE, electrolytes including calcium, magnesium, vitamin B12 and folate)
- Holter ECG
- brain MRI with contrast targeted to the temporal lobes and hippocampal regions
- neurologic reevaluation with test results at the Epilepsy Clinic (write to epilessia.osgb@aslcittaditorino.it)
- refrain from driving

If seizure recurs, return to the ED.
diagnosis_phrase: probable first seizure with possible focal onset and secondary generalization

clinical_note:
This is a patient who presented to the ED for malaise and a finding of sCr 1.9 mg/dL.
In July sCr 0.7 mg/dL; urinalysis negative except for a very high urine specific gravity. In September admission to Cardiology for cardiac ischemia treated with PTCA; discharged on ACE inhibitor and antiplatelet therapy (ticagrelor). The patient reports a cutaneous reaction the day after discharge, treated with an antihistamine. No further cutaneous problems thereafter. Since then, however, persistent generalized malaise with dyspnea on moderate exertion and lower-extremity pain. Recent pulmonology evaluation without specific indications.
From a nephrology standpoint, sCr 1.3 am/dL in early November, 1.9 mg/dL at the most recent check, confirmed in the ED. Urinalysis negative. Concurrent increase in eosinophils (within normal limits in July; 5.9% in October; 13% in November) with the remaining CBC parameters unremarkable. CK within normal limits, no other abnormalities. Physical examination unremarkable, no signs of volume overload. No livedo reticularis.
The pathogenesis of the worsening renal function cannot currently be defined with certainty; an immuno-allergic nephritis cannot be excluded; however, confirmation could only be provided by a histological investigation, which is currently contraindicated due to the need for antiplatelet therapy.
Given the current status, there are therefore no indications for nephrology admission, but for close outpatient monitoring to be arranged based on cardiology recommendations.

BP not measurable. SpO2 95% on RA. Temp 37°C. Infused NS 1000 cc and Dilzene 15 mg for rate control.

On exam: Agitated patient. Hyperkinetic delirium. Speech confused and disjointed. Disoriented to time/place, non-cooperative.
Cardiopulmonary exam: tachyarrhythmic heart sounds. Decreased breath sounds throughout, crackles +.
Peripheral vascular exam: mild bilateral dependent edema of the lower limbs.
Abdomen: protuberant due to adiposity, umbilical hernia, reducible.
Labs: WBC 10, Hb 11, Plt 277, Creat 2, Na 142, CRP 1.6, TnT 0.03
ECG: AF, 160/min, isolated PVC with inferior axis, diffuse ST depression in inferolateral leads -> regression at VR 120/min.
ECHO (VR >140/min): LV severely hypokinetic (EF 20–25%) with diffuse hypokinesia, severe biatrial dilation. RV hypokinetic. Moderate MR. No pericardial effusion. IVC dilated, fixed.

Conclusion:
First finding of atrial fibrillation of unknown duration, with rapid ventricular response. CHA2DS2-VASc 7.
Severe left ventricular systolic impairment newly identified.
Long-standing chest pain with negative troponin (Creat 2). No urgent cardiology indications.

I would recommend:
1) Rate control (I would avoid beta-blockers and calcium-channel antagonists due to EF), start Lanoxin 1 amp IV in 100 cc over 1 h, repeatable; if insufficient, despite AF of unknown duration, I would administer Cordarone IV (4 amps in 250 cc of dextrose at 21 cc/h) to improve VR, accepting the low risk of pharmacologic cardioversion (severely dilated atria), with the aim of avoiding hemodynamic destabilization and consequent inevitable electrical cardioversion.
2) Anticoagulation (Clexane titrated to eGFR)
3) Admission to medical ward, optimization of compensation and therapy, reassessment with echocardiogram (at optimized VR).
diagnosis_phrase: Severe left ventricular systolic impairment newly identified
